explanation: • Assertion (A) – True: o Ibn Battuta records that Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued a new gold coin called Dinar. o He also introduced other coin denominations, including copper and

subject: Medieval History
question: With whose permission did the English set up their first factory in Surat?
explanation: • 1600: Queen Elizabeth I granted a charter to the East India Company to trade in the East. • Captain William Hawkins (1609): o Reached Jahangir’s court and sought permission for trade privileges. o Secured initial concessions, though limited. • 1612: Captain Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese fleet near Surat (Battle of Swally). o This broke Portuguese naval monopoly on the western coast. • 1613: English secured permission from Jahangir to establish their first permanent factory at Surat. • 1615: King James I sent Sir Thomas Roe as ambassador to Jahangir’s court. o Roe secured further trade privileges and allowed the English to set up factories at Ahmedabad, Broach, and Agra. The first English factory at Surat was set up with Jahangir’s permission → Option (b).

subject: Medieval History
question: Among the following, who was not a proponent of Bhakti cult?
explanation: • Nagarjuna (c. 150–250 CE): o A great Buddhist philosopher, founder of the Madhyamaka (Middle Path) school of Mahayana Buddhism. o Propounded the doctrine of Shunyata (emptiness). o Known as the “Second Buddha.” o Not connected with the Bhakti movement. • Tukaram (1608–1649 CE): o Saint of the Bhakti movement in Maharashtra. o Devotee of Vitthala (Vithoba, a form of Krishna/Vishnu). o Known for Abhangas (devotional poetry) and kirtans. • Tyagaraja (1767–1847 CE): o One of the greatest composers of Carnatic music. o Devoted his compositions to Lord Rama. o Central figure in Bhakti through music. • Vallabhacharya (1479–1531 CE): o Founder of the Pushti Marg (Path of Grace) sect of Vaishnavism. o Proponent of Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism) philosophy. o Centered devotion on Krishna of Braj (child form of Shrinathji). Only Nagarjuna was not a Bhakti cult proponent → Option (a).

subject: Medieval History
question: What was the immediate reason for Ahmad Shah Abdali to invade India and fight the Third Battle of Panipat?

options.a: He wanted to avenge the expulsion by Marathas of his viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore
options.b: The frustrated governor of Jullundhar Adina Beg Khan invited him to invade Punjab
options.c: He wanted to punish Mughal administration for non-payment of the revenues of the Chahar Mahal (Gujarat, Aurangabad, Sialkot and Pasrur)
options.d: He wanted to annex all the fertile plains of Punjab up to the borders of Delhi to his kingdom

explanation: Marathas of his viceroy Timur Shah from Lahore • Background: o After the decline of the Mughal Empire (post-Nadir Shah’s invasion, 1739), northern India was fragmented. o The Marathas expanded northward, defeating Abdali’s son Timur Shah, who was Abdali’s viceroy in Lahore. • Immediate Cause: o The Marathas expelled Timur Shah from Lahore. o Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) considered this an insult and decided to retaliate with a full-scale invasion. • Other Contributing Factors: o o o o • Internal Mughal weakness and anarchy. Rivalries between Marathas, Rajputs, Jats, Rohillas, and Nawabs of Awadh. Religious tensions (fear of Maratha Hindu empire). Invitations by Rohilla chief Najib-udDaula and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh encouraged Abdali. Result: o Led to the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) between Marathas and Abdali. o One of the largest battles of the 18th century; Marathas were defeated. o Weakened both sides → paved the way for the rise of the British in India. Correct Answer = (a) Aven

subject: Medieval History
question: Why did Buddhism start declining in India in the early medieval times? 1. Buddha was by that time considered as one of the incarnations of Vishnu and thus became a part of Vaishnavism. 2. The invading tribes from Central Asia till the time of last Gupta king adopted Hinduism and persecuted Buddhists. 3. The Kings of Gupta dynasty were strongly opposed to Buddhism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Statement 1 - Correct o During the Gupta period, Buddha was absorbed into the Hindu pantheon as an avatar of Vishnu. o This assimilation reduced Buddhism’s separate identity → contributed to its decline. • Statement 2 - Incorrect o o Central Asian tribes (Kushanas, later Huns) often adopted Hinduism or sometimes Buddhism. But they did not systematically persecute Buddhists in the Gupta era. • Statement 3 - Incorrect o The Guptas were patrons of Hinduism, but not “strongly opposed” to Buddhism. o Buddhist institutions still existed under Gupta patronage (e.g., Nalanda grew in this period). Other Major Causes of Decline : • Corruption and luxury in Buddhist Sanghas → decline in discipline. • Divisions (Hinayana, Mahayana, Vajrayana, Tantrayana). • Use of Sanskrit instead of Pali/Prakrit → loss of mass appeal. • Revival of Hinduism by Shankaracharya, Ramanuja, Bhakti saints. • Loss of royal patronage after Harshavardhana. • Huna and later Muslim invasions destroyed monasteries like Nala

subject: Medieval History
question: India maintained its early cultural contacts and trade links with Southeast Asia across the Bay of Bengal. For this pre-eminence of early maritime history of Bay of Bengal, which of the following could be the most convincing explanation/explanations?

options.a: As compared to other countries, India had a better shipbuilding technology in ancient and medieval times.
options.b: The rulers of southern India always patronized traders, Brahmin priests and Buddhist monks in this context.
options.c: Monsoon winds across the Bay of Bengal facilitated sea voyages.
options.d: Both (a) and (b) are convincing explanations in this context.

explanation: Shipbuilding technology (a) – Correct o India had advanced shipbuilding and navigation skills, evident from ports like Arikamedu, Tamralipti, and Kaveripattinam. o Indian ships could cross the Bay of Bengal safely for trade and cultural exchange. • Royal patronage (b) – Correct o Southern Indian rulers (Pallavas, Cholas, Pandyas) encouraged maritime trade. o They supported Brahmin priests and Buddhist monks, who carried Indian culture, scripts, religion (Hinduism, Buddhism), and art forms to Southeast Asia. • Monsoon winds (c) – not main reason o Monsoon winds facilitated sea voyages but were a natural phenomenon available to all, not unique to India. o The real edge was India’s shipbuilding superiority + state patronage. Hence, the option (d) Both (a) and (b) is the answer.

subject: Medieval History
question: Consider the following Bhakti Saints : 1. Dadu Dayal 2. Guru Nanak 3. Tyagaraja Who among the above was/were preaching when the Lodi dynasty fell and Babur took over?
explanation: Explanation (Crisp Bullets): • Fall of Lodi Dynasty & Babur’s entry – The First Battle of Panipat (1526) ended the Lodi dynasty and began Mughal rule. • Guru Nanak (1469–1539) – Founder of Sikhism, actively preaching during this time. He travelled widely across India and beyond, spreading the message of equality, devotion, and opposition to rituals. • Dadu Dayal (1544–1603) – Born much later, post-Mughal consolidation under Akbar. • Tyagaraja (1767–1847) – A Carnatic music saint-composer, active in the 18th–19th century, long after the Mughal era. Thus, only Guru Nanak was a contemporary preacher during Babur’s invasion and the fall of the Lodis.

subject: Medieval History
question: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was

options.a: the mosque for the use of Royal Family
options.c: the hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars of various religions.
options.d: the room in which the nobles belonging to different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs

explanation: with scholars of various religions. • Built by Akbar in 1575 at Fatehpur Sikri – Ibadat Khana means House of Worship. • Purpose – To hold debates and discussions with scholars from different religions: Islam, Hinduism, Jainism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, etc. • Outcome – Inspired Akbar’s policy of Sulh-iKul (universal tolerance) and later led to the formation of Din-i-Ilahi (1582). • Significance – Reflected Akbar’s curiosity, statesmanship, and attempt at religious syncretism. Hence, Ibadat Khana was not a mosque or private chamber, but a debating hall for interfaith dialogue.

subject: Medieval History
question: In medieval India, the designations ‘Mahattara’ and ‘Pattakila’ were used for
explanation: • Mahattara (Mahattam) and Pattakila (Patel) were village headmen in medieval India. • They acted as local leaders, responsible for administration, revenue collection, and maintaining law & order in the village. • Worked as intermediaries between villagers and the state authorities. • They also represented the village community in dealings with higher officials. Hence, these designations clearly referred to village headmen, not military, ritual specialists, or guild leaders.

subject: Medieval History
question: With reference to Indian history, which of the following is/are the essential elementary elements of the feudal system? 1. A very strong centralized political authority and a very weak provincial or local political authority 2. Emergence of administrative structure based on control and possession of land 3. Creation of lord-vassal relationship between the feudal lord and his overlord Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: • Feudal system = decentralized power, not centralized → so Statement 1 is incorrect. • Land as the basis of administration & revenue became central → Statement 2 is correct. • Lord–vassal relationship (overlord granting land in return for loyalty/military service) was a core feature → Statement 3 is correct. • In medieval India, land grants to samantas, chiefs, and officials led to the rise of Indian feudalism → weak central power, strong local rulers. Hence, only 2 and 3 are essential elements.

subject: Medieval History
question: Consider the following pairs: Medieval Indian State — Present Region 1. Champaka : Central India 2. Durgara : Jammu 3. Kuluta : Malabar Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
explanation: • Champaka → Refers to Chamba in Himachal Pradesh (north India, Ravi valley), not Central India → Incorrect. • Durgara → Refers to the medieval name for Jammu; modern Dogra identity comes from this → Correct. • Kuluta → Refers to Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh, not Malabar (Kerala) → Incorrect. Thus, only Pair 2 is correctly matched.

subject: Medieval History
question: Consider the following: The arrival of Babur into India led to the 1. Introduction of gunpowder. 2. Introduction of the arch and dome in the region’s architecture. 3. Establishment of Timurid dynasty. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: • Gunpowder (1): Already introduced in India before Babur’s arrival (used by Delhi Sultanate and Vijayanagara kings) → Not due to Babur. • Arch and Dome (2): Introduced much earlier by Delhi Sultans (Qutb-ud-din Aibak, Iltutmish, etc.) in mosques and tombs → Not Babur’s contribution. • Timurid Lineage (3): Babur was a direct descendant of Timur (from father’s side) and Genghis Khan (from mother’s side). He established the Mughal Empire in India (1526), which was essentially a Timurid dynasty branch → Correct. Therefore, only Statement 3 is correct.

subject: Medieval History
question: Who of the following founded a new city on the south bank of a tributary to river Krishna and undertook to rule his new kingdom as the agent of a deity to whom all the land south of the river Krishna was supposed to belong?
explanation: • Harihara I (1336 CE), also called Hakka, along with his brother Bukka Raya, founded Vijayanagar city. • The city was established on the south bank of Tungabhadra River (tributary of Krishna). • Inspired by sage Vidyaranya, Harihara declared himself the agent of the deity Virupaksha (Shiva of Hampi). • His kingdom expanded into former Hoysala territories after the death of Ballala III (1343 CE). • This laid the foundation of the Vijayanagara Empire (Sangama dynasty). Thus, Harihara I was the founder, ruling symbolically as the deity’s servant, not as an independent overlord.

subject: Medieval History
question: With reference to the cultural history of medieval India, consider the following statements : 1. Siddhas (Sittars) of Tamil region were monotheistic and condemned idolatry. 2. Lingayats of Kannada region questioned the theory of rebirth and rejected the caste hierarchy. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Siddhas / Sittars (Tamil region): o Flourished around Sangam period onwards. o Advocated monotheism, condemned idol worship and ritualism. o Emphasized direct spiritual realization and mystical practices. • Lingayats (Kannada region, 12th c.) o Founded by Basaveshwara. o Rejected rebirth theory → believed true Lingayats attain moksha in this life. o Condemned caste hierarchy, male– female inequality, and ritual orthodoxy. o Promoted Vachana literature (simple Kannada prose-poetry). Both statements are correct → hence Option (c).

subject: Medieval History
question: Banjaras during the medieval period of Indian history were generally—
explanation: • Banjaras → largest nomadic trading community of medieval India. • Name derived from Sanskrit “Banaj / Vanijya” = Trade. • Main role → transportation of food grains & commodities across towns and villages. • They also supplied raw materials (cotton, indigo, salt, etc.) to mandis (markets). • Alauddin Khalji settled Banjaras on the banks of Yamuna near Delhi to ensure regular supply of food-grains to the capital. • Integral part of inter-local trade & logistics during medieval India. Hence, they were traders, not agriculturists, warriors, or weavers.

subject: Medieval History
question: With reference to the economic history of medieval India the term ‘Araghatta’ refers to—

options.b: Land grants made to military officers
options.c: Waterwheel used in the irrigation of land

explanation: • Araghatta = ancient Indian term for the Persian wheel. • Meaning: “Ara” (spoke) + “Ghatta” (pot) → device with spokes and pots to lift water. • Operated by draught animals (bullocks, camels, elephants) moving in circles. • Used mainly to lift water from wells for irrigation. • In medieval North India, it was also called Rahat / Reghat. • Different from: o Noria → river/stream-powered water wheel. o Saqia → Persian bucket pump system for wells. Hence, Araghatta was crucial in pre-modern irrigation technology.

subject: Medieval History
question: Which one of the following was a very important seaport in the Kakatiya kingdom?
explanation: • The Kakatiyas ruled Andhradesa roughly from 10th century to early 14th century CE. • Initially feudatories of the Rashtrakutas → later of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani → finally emerged as an independent power. • Motupalli (in present-day Andhra Pradesh) was their chief seaport. • The port was famous for trade in horses, elephants, pearls, and diamonds. • It was visited by Marco Polo, the Venetian traveller, during his journey to the East. • Motupalli connected the Kakatiya kingdom to Southeast Asia and China, boosting maritime trade. Hence option b is correct.

subject: Medieval History
question: Consider the following statements: 1. In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate, the in-charge of revenue collection was known as ‘Amil’. 2. The Iqta system of Sultans of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution. 3. The office of ‘Mir Bakshi’ came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Statement 1 is correct: In the land revenue system of the Delhi Sultanate, the central government appointed amil to collect revenues in each subdivision called shiq. • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Iqta system of land control was first introduced in the Delhi Sultanate by Iltutmish. The institution known by its Arabic name, iqta, had existed in the early Islamic world as a means of rewarding services to the state. It was not an ancient indigenous institution. • Statement 3 is incorrect: The office of Mir Bakshi was established under the Mughal empire, who was head of the military • department, nobility, information and intelligence agencies. Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Medieval History
question: Consider the following statements: 1. Saint Nimbarka was a contemporary of Akbar. 2. Saint Kabir was greatly influenced by Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Statement 1 is incorrect: Saint Nimbarka is believed to be the contemporary of Ramanuja (11th century). He believed in total devotion to Krishna and Rama. The Mughal emperor Akbar lived from 1542–1605. Nimbarkacharya also known as Nimbarka, Nimbaditya or Niyamananda, was a Hindu philosopher and theologian and the chief proponent of Dvaitadvaita. He wrote Dashasloki and Vedanta. He was also a prominent astronomer. • Statement 2 is incorrect: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi (1564–1624 AD) was an Islamic scholar of the Naqshbandi silsilah. Kabir (1440–1510 AD) was a follower of Nirguna bhakti of the 15th century. • Hence, option (d) is correct.

subject: Medieval History
question: With reference to Mughal India, what is/are the difference/differences between Jagirdar and Zamindar? 1. Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties, whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection. 2. Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary and revenue rights or Zamindars were not hereditary. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: • Statement 1 is incorrect: Zamindars were also expected to maintain law and order in their jurisdictions. The judicial and police functions were performed locally by zamindars. • Statement 2 is incorrect: Jagirdar only has the right to claim and enjoy the revenue collected from the land. Jagirs were transferable and could be seized too. • Additional information: o The holder of land was termed Zamindar. They have hereditary rights over the land. o The primary responsibility of zamindars was to collect revenue and deposit it in the royal treasury. o Law and order were another duty imposed on zamindars in their jurisdictions. The local zamindars handled the police and judicial duties. o The Jagirdars were the King’s appointed officials who were given land by the King. The jagir system allocated a certain amount of land to each person, without any inheritance rights. o Jagirdar is only entitled to claim and enjoy the revenue collected from the land. Jagirs could be transferred and seized

question: With reference to Mian Tansen, which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.a: Tansen was the title given to him by Emperor Akbar.
options.b: Tansen composed Dhrupada on Hindu gods and goddesses.
options.c: Tansen composed songs for his patrons.

explanation: • Correct answer is Option (a): Tansen was the title given to him by Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior. • Raja Ram Chandra of Bandavagarh employed Tansen as a court musician at his darbar (Rewa). • After learning of Tansen’s extraordinary talent, Akbar wrote the king of Rewa a “firman” requesting Tansen and appointed him as one of the Navaratnas in his court. He bestowed upon him the name “Mian.” According to Lalita Ramakrishna’s Musical Heritage of India, Tansen is also referred to as the “Sangit Samrat.” • He composed various dhrupads on Rama, Parvati, Shiva, and Ganesha. A compilation of 300 of his dhrupad that were in Gauhar Bani is called Kalpadruma. Tansen composed his favorite ragas — Multani, Bhairavi and Todi. • He created the ragas Darbari Kanhra for the night, Mian Ki Todi for the morning, Mian ki Sarang for the midday, and Mian ki Malhar for the season. • His descendants and disciples are called Seniyas. He composed songs for his patrons. • Hence, option (a) is correct.

subject: Medieval History
question: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to albums and individual portraits?
explanation: • Correct answer is Option (c): Mughal Emperor Jahangir shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to albums and individual portraits. • • • • The Mughal school of painting achieved increased charm, elegance, and grandeur during his rule. The portrait of Jahangir, who is pictured holding a picture of the Virgin Mary in his right hand, is the best representation of this time period. Ayar-i-Danish and Anwar-i-sunavli are two further animal fable books with illustrations that date to Jahangir’s reign. Hence, option (c) is correct.

question: Consider the following events in the history of India: 1. Rise of Pratiharas under King Bhoja 2. Establishment of Pallava power under Mahendravarman-I 3. Establishment of Chola power by Purantaka 4. Pala dynasty founded by Gopala What is the correct chronological order of the above events, starting from the earliest time?
explanation: • Correct chronology of given events are as follows: 2-4-1-3 • King / Dynasty / Duration / Founder o Mahendravarman I — Pallavas — 600–630 CE o Gopala — Palas — 750 CE — (founder: Gopala; later Dharmapala) o King Bhoja — Gurjara-Pratiharas — Mihir Bhoja (836–885 CE) o Parantaka I — Cholas — (Parantaka’s reign c. 907–953 CE); Vijayalaya earlier founded Chola ascendancy • Explanation: o The Pallavas were powerful in southern India between the 6th and 9th centuries, with Mahendravarman I (c. 600–630) a notable early ruler. o • The Pala Empire was established when Gopala was chosen as ruler in 750 CE. o The Gurjara-Pratiharas rose under rulers like Nagabhata I and reached prominence under Mihir Bhoja (9th century). o The Cholas rose to prominence later; Parantaka I reigned in the early 10th century. Hence, option (c) is correct.

question: Consider the following statements: 1. It was during the reign of Iltutmish that Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in pursuit of the fugitive Khwarezm prince. 2. It was during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq that Taimur occupied Multan and crossed the Indus. 3. It was during the reign of Deva Raya II of the Vijayanagara Empire that Vasco da Gama reached the coast of Kerala. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Statement 1 is correct. In his pursuit of the fugitive Khwarezm prince, Chengiz Khan arrived in India during the reign of Iltutmish. By denying shelter to Prince Jalaluddhin of Central Asia, Iltutmish protected India from Chengiz Khan’s fury. • Statement 2 is incorrect. The period of Muhammad bin Tughlaq was from 1325 to 1351. Taimur invaded India during the reign of Nasir-ud-din Muhammad Shah (1394– 1412), the last Tughlaq ruler. • Statement 3 is incorrect. The reign of Devaraya II lasted from 1422 to 1426. He died in 1446. Vasco da Gama came to India in 1498. • hence option a correct

question: With reference to Indian history, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The Nizamat of Arcot emerged from Hyderabad. 2. The Mysore Kingdom emerged from the Vijayanagara Empire. 3. Rohilkhand Kingdom was formed out of the territories occupied by Ahmad Shah Durrani. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation: • Statement 1 is incorrect: The kingdom of Arcot, also known as the kingdom of Carnatic, was the monarchy that ruled over the majority of the eastern part of the presentday Tamil Nadu region throughout the eighteenth century. • Statement 2 is correct: Under the Vijayanagar Empire, there was a small feudal kingdom called Mysore. The ruling Wodeyar dynasty declared their independence following the fall of Vijayanagar in 1565, and Raja Wodeyar ascended the throne in 1578. The capital moved from Mysore to Srirangapatna in 1610. • Statement 3 is incorrect: Ali Muhammad Khan established Rohilkhand, a small kingdom, by taking advantage of the breakdown of authority in North India following Nadir Shah’s invasion. • hence option b correct

question: According to Portuguese writer Nuniz, the women in Vijayanagara Empire were experts in which of the following areas? 1. Wrestling 2. Astrology 3. Accounting 4. Soothsaying Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation: • Correct answer is Option (d): According to Fernao Nuniz: “he (the king of Vijaynagar) also has women who wrestle, do accounting and others who are astrologers and soothsayers. • Fernao Nuniz was a Portuguese traveler who visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya. He has recorded that in Vijayanagara society, women typically held prominent positions, and there are numerous examples of them actively participating in the political, social, and literary life of the kingdom. • In addition to receiving training in wrestling, using swords and shields, music, and other fine arts, some of these women also had some exposure to literature. • hence option d correct

question: With reference to medieval India, which one of the following is the correct sequence in ascending order in terms of size?
explanation: • Correct answer is Option (a): o The correct order according to the size is: Pargana > Sarkar > Suba. o The entire Suba was split into Sarkars (districts), with a military commander known as the chief Shiqdar in charge of each one. Each Sarkar was divided into smaller units called Parganas. o Each Pargana had two Karkuns (clerks or writers), one Fotahdar (treasurer), one Shiqdar (military officer), one Amin or Munsif (civilian judge). o • In order to organise his kingdom for better administration and taxation, Akbar adopted Sher Shah’s methods and principles. hence option a correct

question: With reference to Indian history, consider the following statements: 1. The first Mongol invasion of India happened during the reign of Jalalud-din Khalji. 2. During the reign of Ala-ud-din Khalji, one Mongol assault marched up to Delhi and besieged the city. 3. Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq temporarily lost portions of the north-west of his kingdom to Mongols. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: • Statement 1 is incorrect: The first Mongol invasion of India took place in the reign of Sultan Shams-ud-din Iltutmish. • Statement 2 is correct: During the reign of Ala-ud-din Khalji, one of the Mongol invasions reached till the outskirts of Delhi city and besieged it. Alauddin established a huge permanent, standing army to satisfy his ambition of conquest and to protect the country from Mongol invasion. The Mongols attacked at the worst time possible for Alauddin Khilji – when he was busy laying siege to Chittor. Alauddin Khilji was forced to retreat to Siri for about two months. The Mongols attacked and pillaged not only the surrounding areas, but Delhi itself. Alauddin Khilji continued to hold the fortress at Siri; Targhi withdrew the siege after a few months and left the area. • Statement 3 is incorrect: Muhammad-binTughlaq defeated the Mongols and he had not lost any of the portions of his kingdom to them. Hence option b correct.

question: The world’s second tallest statue in sitting pose of Ramanuja was inaugurated by the Prime Minister of India at Hyderabad recently. Which one of the following statements correctly represents the teachings of Ramanuja?

options.a: The best means of salvation was devotion.
options.b: Vedas are eternal, self-existent and wholly authoritative.
options.c: Logical arguments were essential means for the highest bliss.
options.d: Salvation was to be obtained through meditation.

explanation: • Correct answer is Option (a): Shri Ramanujacharya firmly believed that intense devotion to Vishnu was the best means to attain salvation. Sri Ramanujacharya was born in 1017 CE in Tamil Nadu. • He is the most respected Acharya in the philosophy of Sri Vaishnavism. Ramanuja was deeply influenced by the Alvars. He firmly believed that intense devotion to Vishnu was the best means to attain He is famous as the chief proponent of Vishishtadvaita subschool of Vedānta. • He was also referred to as Ilaya Perumal, which means the radiant He wrote nine works that came to be known as the Navratnas including three major commentaries, the Vedartha-Sangraha, the Sribhasya and the Bhagavad Gita-bhashya aimed at providing a philosophical foundation for devotional worship. Vishishtadvaita is a non-dualistic school of Vedanta philosophy in which Brahman alone exists, but is characterized by multiplicity. Hence option a correct.

question: With reference to ancient South India, Korkai, Poompuhar and Muchiri were well known as
explanation: • Korkai: Situated in the Thoothukudi district of Tamil Nadu, Korkai emerged as a significant port city during ancient times, notably flourishing during the era of Tamil Sangam literature. It served as the primary port for the Pandya Kingdom during this period. • Poompuhar: Alternatively known as Kaveripattinam, it stands out as an ancient port city with a vibrant maritime trading legacy. Positioned on the banks of the Kaveri River in Nagapattinam district, it served as the primary port of the Chola Kingdom. • Muchiri: Also referred to as Muziris, it was an ancient port city situated in what is now Kerala, close to Kodungallur. It held substantial importance as a trading hub within the Indian Ocean trade network throughout ancient and medieval eras. Tondi and Muchiri emerged as pivotal ports within the realm of the Chera kingdom. • Hence, all the three sites mentioned were well known as Ports in ancient South India. Hence option b correct.

question: Consider the following dynasties: 1. Hoysala 2. Gahadavala 3. Kakatiya 4. Yadava How many of the above dynasties established their kingdoms in the early eighth century AD?
explanation: • Hoysala Dynasty: Originating from the Indian subcontinent, the Hoysala Empire held sway over much of present-day Karnataka from the 10th to the 14th centuries. Their capital shifted from Belur to Halebidu. • Gahadavala Dynasty: After the fall of the Pratihara Empire, several Rajput states emerged. Among these, the Gahadavalas of Kanauj (12th–13th century) were prominent. • Kakatiya Dynasty: Ruled over present-day Telangana and Andhra Pradesh during the 12th–14th centuries with Warangal as the capital. Their architecture is seen in the Thousand Pillar Temple and Ramappa Temple. • Yadava Dynasty: The Yadavas ruled during the 12th–14th centuries, in present-day Maharashtra, with their capital at Devagiri (Daulatabad). • Hence, none of the above dynasties were established in the early eighth century AD. Hence option d correct.

question: Who among the following rulers of medieval Gujarat surrendered Diu to the Portuguese?
explanation: • Amidst increasing Portuguese threats to Gujarat’s trade and coastal regions, the Sultan of Gujarat sought Ottoman support, leading to exchanges between the two powers. • The Ottomans ousted the Portuguese from the Red Sea and dispatched a fleet to aid Bahadur Shah of Gujarat. Rumi Khan, an Ottoman commander, successfully repelled Portuguese attacks on Daman and Diu in 1531. • However, facing a larger threat from the Mughals, Bahadur Shah granted Bassein and allowed the Portuguese to construct a fort at Diu as part of a defensive alliance, solidifying their presence in Gujarat. • The Treaty of 1534 marked the end of Islamic rule on the Islands of Bombay, as Bahadur Shah formally surrendered Diu to the Portuguese. Hence option c correct.

question: Who among the following rulers of Vijayanagara Empire constructed a large dam across Tungabhadra River and a canal-cum-aqueduct several kilometres long from the river to the capital city?
explanation: • The Vijayanagar Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty. • Four dynasties ruled Vijayanagar — Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu (1336–1672 CE). • Deva Raya I (c. 1406–1422 CE) of the Sangama dynasty was a capable ruler known for his military exploits and support for irrigation works. • He constructed a dam across the Tungabhadra River to bring canals into the city to relieve the water shortage. • He also built a dam on the river Haridra for irrigation purposes. • Several foreign travelers such as Ibn Battuta, Nicolo de Conti, Abdur Razzak, and Domingo Paes visited the empire and recorded these achievements. Hence option a correct.

question: Who of the following rulers of medieval India gave permission to the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal?
explanation: • Emperor Krishnadevaraya allowed the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal in 1510 CE. • The town was named Bhatakala after the Jain grammarian Bhattakalanka Deva, who hailed from Haduvalli, 16 km away — the capital of the Saluvas of Gerusoppa. Hence option a correct.

subject: Medieval History
question: Who among the following led a successful military campaign against the kingdom of Srivijaya, the powerful maritime State, which ruled the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java and the neighbouring islands?
explanation: • Rajendra Chola I (reigned c. 1014–1044 CE), also known as Rajendra the Great, was one of the most powerful emperors of the Chola dynasty. • He is famous for his ambitious military expeditions that went far beyond the Indian subcontinent. • The historical records highlight his “overseas campaign” involving both his army and navy against the kingdom of Srivijaya, a dominant maritime empire that ruled over Sumatra, Java, the Malay Peninsula, and surrounding islands. • This campaign, launched in the early 11th century, demonstrated the naval supremacy of the Chola Empire and aimed to protect and expand the Chola’s trade interests in Southeast Asia. • His victory over Srivijaya earned him the title “Kadaram Kondan” (Conqueror of Kadaram — modern-day Kedah in Malaysia, part of Srivijaya). Hence option c correct.
